name: Hangor and Khukri, 9 December 1971
status: DRAFT for SME review: built from public accounts, not yet confirmed
summary: The first sinking of a warship by a submarine since 1945. Hangor, submerged west of Diu Head, fired three torpedoes at the two Indian frigates hunting her: the first, at Kirpan, missed (or failed); a second hit Khukri, which sank within minutes with heavy loss of life; a third was fired at Kirpan, which withdrew. Hangor escaped despite a prolonged search.
assumptions: Start about 14:00 UTC (19:30 local), after dark; Hangor already in contact and submerged at 50 m.
Khukri steers west at 12 kn; Kirpan keeps station 4 km on her starboard bow (the public accounts give the frigates as searching at slow speed; the formation is an assumption).
Positions are approximate (about 35 nm SSW of Diu); the accounts disagree by several miles.

The torpedoes are the database's generic heavyweight torpedo (WPN-TORP-HW), not the French E14/E15 the boat carried; their reliability and the 'first torpedo did not explode' account are not modelled.
The Indian frigates' sonar (Type 170/174) is the generic hull-mounted medium-frequency sonar.
The engagement window is one hour; the Indian search of the following days is not modelled.

measures.name: Torpedoes fired by Hangor
measures.note: Three by most accounts; the first is reported to have run deep or failed to detonate.

measures.name: Time to Hangor's first hit (s)
measures.note: Not in the record to the minute: about ten minutes after the attack began is an estimate for the SMEs to confirm or replace.
